relevance_note: Letter describing one adult with a GFAP variant in an alternative transcript: "Subsequent research whole exome sequencing (WES) detected a pathogenic variant" (NM_001131019.2(GFAP):c.1289G > A; p.(Arg430His)).
method_note: Built by hand-written Python dict (no table transcription; the paper has no tables). In scope: the single unnamed patient ('patient'), his affected mother and maternal uncle (described in relation to him; neither was genotyped, so no variant rows), and the two individuals of reference [2] said to carry the same variant ('This variant has been previously reported in two affected individuals'); they are included because the variant is an individual-level fact, labelled 'ref [2] patient' and 'ref [2] patient 2'; their HDAC6 variant is not described so has no row. The patient's GFAP variant is printed in two transcripts in one sentence: canonical-transcript deep intronic 'c.1171 + 472G > A' and alternative-transcript 'NM_001131019.2(GFAP):c.1289G > A; p.(Arg430His)'; read as one variant and recorded once using the alternative-transcript string; the canonical description is not in any field. No zygosity, inheritance or variant type is stated for this person (intro statement on heterozygous mutations is general). Mother is affected but untested, so inheritance not reported. ACVRL1 VUS recorded as a second variant row for the patient (attributed unambiguously). Patient's normal neurological examination: the specific named absences (gait abnormality, abnormal posture, dysarthria) recorded as excluded; 'normal neurological examination' recorded as excluded 'abnormal neurological examination' and 'asymptomatic'/'other symptoms related to AD' used to exclude nothing more specific. Checklist 'dysarthria or dysphonia' and 'ataxia or cerebellar signs' left not reported for the patient (narrower absences only). Fig. 1 MRI findings are attributed to the patient via 'a brain MRI demonstrated findings previously described in adult-onset AD (Fig. 1)'. 'No changes were noted in the subcortical regions' recorded as an excluded feature but does not exclude the broader checklist item cerebral white matter abnormality. Uncle's vital status 'deceased' is inferred from the mention of his autopsy. n_patients_reported=1 is not a stated count; the letter describes one patient first-hand. No contradictions found.
